messages:
monitoring-bot: ALERT — region-west4 control-plane heartbeat gap detected. 90% API servers NACKing, pod eviction spikes on gpu pools, p95 latency spike >1200ms. auto-escalation to incidents channel.

lina_oncall: observed a sudden surge in node evictions + control plane 503s. External LB still passing traffic but health checks failing.

charlie_sre: i'm on it. checking control plane API reachability and etcd status. first guess: network flap + api server overload.

maia_ops: i'm seeing telemetry showing consistent thermal throttling on gpus in west4, concurrent with BGP withdraw events from two ISPs. could be correlated.

nathan_infra: runbook start: verify api-server endpoints and leader.

charlie_sre: ran quick checks — api-server pods show CrashLoopBackOff on 6/8 control-plane nodes. etcd endpoints partially healthy (3/5). mounting kube-apiserver logs:

```
E0321 14:07:12.123456 1 node_controller.go:512] Node eviction: node gpu-node-22 reason: network-unreachable
W0321 14:08:01.654321 1 apiserver.go:234] Failed to serve: listen tcp 0.0.0.0:6443: bind: cannot assign requested address
```

charlie_sre: this looks like ephemeral network interface flaps causing apiserver bind errors.

katie_network: confirmed: route leak at provider edge caused partial control-plane isolation for west4 for ~3m. Provider says they pushed a fix ~2m ago but we're seeing lingering flaps.

maia_ops: meanwhile GPU daemonset shows mass evictions due to thermal-tripping on a subset of racks: temps jumped then NVML reported driver aborts. likely workload spike routed to a few racks during the flap.

lina_oncall: impact: hosted API clients in region-west4 experiencing 100% errors for inference endpoints. Failover policy configured to try nearest region (west3) but we see slow draining and some requests still queuing.

charlie_sre: action plan (short): 1) fail traffic away from west4 at global LB (init manual failover), 2) set Dedicated spare pool warm-up in west3 (scale up + reserve GPUs), 3) run cluster control-plane recovery: cordon problematic masters and restart apiserver systemd unit after network stabilizes, 4) postmortem collection.

maia_ops: i'm starting a graceful traffic shift now. @nathan_infra please prepare capacity in west3: add 12 gpus to reserved pool and ensure quantized model variants available to reduce footprint.

nathan_infra: scaling reserved pool:
```
# terraform apply snippet (scaled reserved-gpu-pool)
module "reserved_pool_west3" {
  source = "./modules/pool"
  gpu_count = 12
  size = "p3xlarge"
}
```

nathan_infra: kicked off infra changes, ETA ~6m for instance boot + model warm start.

katie_network: i applied emergency route filter to stop the leak for west4 and validated BGP convergence with both peers. provider confirmed stable.

charlie_sre: attempting control-plane restart sequence on affected masters now. will coordinate with ops to not cause split-brain.

lina_oncall: please post short user-facing note to status page: saying degraded/unavailable for region-west4 and failover in progress. minimal details. i'll draft.

maia_ops: status update: traffic cutover initiated at global LB — 92% of traffic moved to west3/west2. error rate for clients dropping. monitoring shows request queue depth returning to normal.

charlie_sre: control-plane apis back to stable on remaining masters. recovered etcd quorum after 2 nodes rejoined. marking east-west4 maintenance window for deeper investigation.

lina_oncall: incident classified as REGION_CONTROL_PLANE_ISOLATION + THERMAL_GPU_EVICITIONS. Next: post-incident RCA to include provider route filters, LB failover tuning, and thermal mitigation (spread/cooling/auto-shed). Thanks team. :thumbsup:

monitoring-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — severity: P1 -> P2, duration so far ~18m.
